title: How to Choose a Music Service for Your Store | Entuned
meta_description: How to choose a music service for your retail store. What to evaluate — licensing, contracts, measurement — and how Mood Media, Soundtrack, and Entuned compare.

faq.q: What is the best music service for a retail store?
faq.a: There's no single best — it depends on what you're optimizing. Mood Media is the enterprise default for fleets that need legal music in hundreds of locations fast. Soundtrack Your Brand is the modern catalog choice with month-to-month billing. Cloud Cover is the budget option. SiriusXM is the familiar-brand pick. And the newer original-music category (Entuned) is built for stores that want fit and measurable outcomes over the biggest library. For a small owner-operator, fit and no contract usually matter more than catalog size.

faq.q: What should I evaluate before signing up for a store music service?
faq.a: Seven things. Licensing coverage — does it include ASCAP, BMI, SESAC, and GMR. Contract length and the early-termination penalty. True per-location cost, all-in, after hardware and support fees bundle. How well you can fit the sound to your specific customer and outcome. Whether it offers any measurement of the music's effect on sales. How fast setup is. And whether anyone can own the outcome it produces. Most services answer the first three and quietly skip the rest.

faq.q: How much does a retail music service cost?
faq.a: Published self-serve pricing runs roughly $17 to $54 per location per month (2026). Cloud Cover Music is the low end at about $17 to $30, SiriusXM for Business is $26.95, Soundtrack Your Brand is $29 to $54, and Mood Media's self-serve plans are $17 to $40 (all vendor published pricing, 2026) — though enterprise and managed installs are custom-quoted and contract-based, and the sticker rarely matches the invoice once hardware and support fees bundle in. QSIC is enterprise, quote-only. Entuned offers a free tier with no card, Boost at $99, and Pro at $399 per location per month. The catalog services generally don't sell measurement as part of the subscription.

faq.q: Do I need the biggest music catalog for my store?
faq.a: Almost never. A hundred-million-track library sounds like the strongest pitch, but a small store will pick one station that sounds roughly right and let it loop — so catalog size buys nothing and fit to your customer buys everything. The research shows what moves the floor is fit, not variety: Areni and Kim (1993) found musical fit shifts willingness to pay, and Milliman (1982) found tempo moves dwell. Both depend on the sound matching your customer, not on library size.

faq.q: How is Entuned different from Mood Media or Soundtrack Your Brand?
faq.a: Three structural differences. There's no licensing to cover — the music is original and PRO-indemnified, so ASCAP and BMI don't apply. There's no contract, and the free tier needs no card. And the music is engineered at the parameter level against your customer and a chosen outcome, then measured on its effect in the store, rather than chosen from a genre menu and reported on by play count. It's not the right fit for stores where music is a curated taste signal, but it's built for practical retail where music is a lever.

faq.q: Can I switch music services if I'm in a contract?
faq.a: Often, but check the terms first. Multi-year enterprise or managed deals — like Mood Media's larger installs — typically carry early-termination penalties, so pull the contract and find the renewal date and exit language before you're inside the auto-renew window. Self-serve and month-to-month services like Mood Media's self-serve tiers, Soundtrack Your Brand, and Cloud Cover Music let you leave anytime. Trying a no-contract option like Entuned Free alongside your current service is a zero-risk way to compare before committing, since it needs no card and has no time limit.
